name: Lip Texture Detail
description: Examines lip surface micro-textures including vermilion border sharpness and mucosal moisture patterns to detect the smoothed-over detail loss common in talking-face synthesis models.
algorithm: Lip Texture Detail — Pixel-Level Spatial Analysis
mechanism:
This method analyzes lip texture rendering detail for deepfake detection:

1. **Lip Region Extraction**: The lip region is precisely segmented per frame using lip landmarks (vermilion border, cupid's bow, lip corners, oral commissures). Both the dry lip surface and wet inner lip are analyzed.

2. **Lip Surface Texture Analysis**: Natural lips show characteristic surface texture: vertical wrinkle lines (more prominent on lower lip), moisture-dependent specularity, and color variation from vermilion border to inner mucosa. The method analyzes texture quality at multiple scales. AI-generated lips often show either over-smoothed surfaces (lacking natural lip wrinkles) or artificial texture patterns.

3. **Lip-Teeth-Tongue Rendering**: When the mouth opens during speech, teeth and tongue become visible. The method evaluates rendering quality of these elements: (a) teeth should show individual tooth structure with correct dental anatomy, (b) tongue position should be consistent with articulated phonemes. AI generators often produce blurred or merged teeth and simplified tongue rendering.

4. **Lip Moisture and Specular Reflection**: Natural lips show moisture-dependent specularity that changes with lip movement (stretching reduces moisture, licking increases it). The method tracks specular patterns — AI generators typically don't model dynamic lip moisture, producing static or absent specular highlights.

5. **Temporal Texture Consistency**: Lip texture should remain consistent across frames — the wrinkle pattern is stable, only varying in visibility with lip stretch. The method tracks lip texture features over time. Frame-to-frame texture instability — changing wrinkle patterns, flickering detail — indicates per-frame independent generation.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through lip texture detail analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video
